catalog_quote: [p.216] All Bs speech varieties except some dialects of Kuy and Tsg retain phonemic accent. The following minimal pair is found in all dialects and establishes contrastive accent for PBS: púnuq [pú:nǔq] tree trunk < PBS *púnuq and punúq [pǔnúq] full < PBS *punúq. ... [p.218] 8.10.2. Factors Influencing the Placement of Accent (1) CANONICAL FORM. In all Bs dialects studied, a closed penult is stressed. Thus, stress is predictable from the shape of the form: all dialects síŋsiŋ ring < PBS *síŋsiŋ, all dialects búkbuk weevil < PBS *búkbuk. Regardless of the accent on the base form, if morphophonemic changes produce a form with a CVC-penult, the penult is stressed. ... (3) ACCENT PAIRS of verb stems and their stative counterparts are found throughout Bs ... War, Ceb, Sur, But lútuq : ... War, Ceb, Sur, But lutúq cooked ... [p.50] The accentual systems of all other Bs dialects have phonetic …

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every quoted sentence and the locators (pp.216, 218, 50; pdf = book + 24) were confirmed verbatim on the held page images of Zorc 1977. (2) Deciding source: a 1977 comparative-historical survey of Bisayan (PL C-44) whose accent statements are pan-Bisayan but explicitly include Sur (accent pair lútuq : lutúq cited for Sur, p.218; Sur not among the varieties that lost accent, 8.10.1). (3) Web/bibliographic sweep (CiNii, Crossref, Glottolog, UPD Linguistics site; general search engines unreachable) found one open Surigaonon-specific phonology article, Dumanig 2015, fetched sources and read: sec. 4.3 p.6 states stress placement 'changes the meaning of the word' and tabulates six penult-vs-final minimal pairs, independently confirming LEXICAL/WORD for Surigaonon proper; it is silent on the CVC-penult sub-rule and on length, so the secondary/weight fields continue to rest on Zorc alon

sources.quote: 'The stress in Surigaonon is indicated by an apostrophe (') where the stressed syllable is always given more emphasis by increasing the pitch and loudness. In some cases, the change of stressed syllable also changes the meaning of the word.' Table 6 lists 'Penultimate Stressed Words' vs 'Final Stressed Words' minimal pairs: buyag 'separate (adj.)' : buyag 'to separate'; waya? 'none' : waya 'left'; amo 'master' : amo? 'monkey'; buhi? 'to free' : buhi? 'alive'; uban 'white hair' : uban 'accompany'; tuyo? 'spill' : tuyo 'three'. 'there are words in the Surigaonon language that are spelled similar
